headline.text: Kanta-Häme's overlapping crude shares lag nationally in symptomatic treatment (34.2%, 95% CI 30.4–38.3 vs 39.5%) and no treatment record within 12 months (32.1%, 95% CI 28.3–36.1 vs 27.5%).

details.text: Kanta-Häme's crude share of patients with no treatment record within 12 months is 32.1% (95% CI 28.3–36.1; n=175/546), whose 95% confidence interval excludes and lies above the national 27.5% (4089/14873); this category mixes untreated patients and treatment that was not recorded.

The crude symptomatic treatment share is 34.2% (95% CI 30.4–38.3; n=187/546), with a 95% confidence interval excluding and falling below the national 39.5% (5871/14873); because these overlapping treatment categories accompany an above-national crude no-treatment-record share (32.1%, 95% CI 28.3–36.1 vs 27.5%), low treatment shares may partly reflect unrecorded treatment.

Across overlapping treatment categories where a patient can receive several treatments, the crude curative share of 23.4% (95% CI 20.1–27.2; n=128/546) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally and crude life-prolonging share of 32.2% (95% CI 28.4–36.3; n=176/546) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) nationally have 95% confidence intervals that include the national values.

The crude share with a recorded MDT meeting is 21.6% (95% CI 18.4–25.3; n=118/546), whose 95% confidence interval excludes and exceeds the national 6.0% (893/14873), but MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures procedures only from direct patient contacts.

headline.text: A journal article shows about 90% diagnosis concordance in HILMO, but table treatment shares lack age and stage adjustment, and public data omit pathway timestamps.

details.text: County shares such as Kanta-Häme's crude 23.4% (95% CI 20.1–27.2; n=128/546) curative share have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted—age-adjusted values exist only in Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, with digitised national lines at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (about ±0.5 percentage points)—and separately cannot be stage-adjusted because stage is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article reports that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, concerning diagnosis concordance only rather than treatment, referral, or MDT recording, while Finland has no cancer quality registry and lung cancer data reporting, collection, and storage remain incomplete.

In public data, primary care visits are not included in the report's data and occupational health is not mentioned, symptoms and referrals are unmeasured, imaging appears only indirectly as clinical-only diagnosis in about 20% of cases without waits, and specialist visits (93.6%) and treatments within 12 months lack start dates.

Only preliminary, unpublished national figures describe pathway durations, averaging 155 days from initial symptoms to treatment in Finland compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, split into 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions with handover alerts, and standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination.

details.text: Given Kanta-Häme's crude no-treatment-record share of 32.1% (95% CI 28.3–36.1; n=175/546) versus 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally and about 48% missing stage, the team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding; the STM roadmap (measure 3.2.1) plans a quality registry decree by 2026–2028 and reports by 2029–2031 at 90% coverage.

Because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national access monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting access times from referral to treatment start using THL 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers with handover alerts, while the STM roadmap (measure 3.1.2) plans national pathway descriptions and access times by 2026–2028 and 2029–2031.

To address the mentor insight that weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings, the team recommends adopting a standard referral template and persistent-symptoms rule after a normal X-ray modelled on KYS's regional pathway document, while the Filha programme's national diagnostics recommendation with primary-care referral criteria and recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because reviewed regional pathway documents name no diagnostic-phase contact person, the team recommends assigning a named contact from referral to diagnosis; at the national level, the STM roadmap plans standardised referral criteria and symptom-based models by 2026–2028 and 2029–2031 (measure 2.5.2) and care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031 (measure 1.2.3).
